title: The Point of No Return
description:
The "supposedly" has been stripped away, as this is the literal final trimester. No more safety nets, no more "next time." (if all goes well, that is.)

The RNG teammates have been rolled, and the results are... well, they're characters.

Some fresh faces, while others are familiar. But the common theme is that they are all... interesting. I guess that's what makes it fun, right? (I hope so.)


Juggling 20 credit hours while FYP looms like a final boss in its second phase.

I’ve gone from "holding the line" to being the line itself.

Faced some of that "wrath" I anticipated at the start of the month.

It turns out, when you stop trying to glue the fractures of other people's expectations and just focus on your own survival, people get loud.

Let them. My exclusion zone is now a fortress. Keep the noise out, and the focus in, just like how Kaname Raana does it.

Wake up, do my own things, not disturb others (hopefully), go off.

Physically, I'm just a vessel for food and code. Socially, I’m a ghost in the machine — more Mutsumi Wakaba than anything — quiet, detached, and not really part of the scene.

But academically? I’m speedrunning towards that July finish line because I can already hear society knocking on the door, and I’d rather open it on my own terms.

Everything is converging. The tasks are stacking. The pressure is peak.

3 assignments due in May, many Tests & Projects in June, and FYP2 presentation in July. It’s like I’m on a rollercoaster that’s just about to drop, and there’s no way to get off.

But if I don't break now, I never will.

May the force be with me.

title: Hurt, but Intact.
description:
May felt like living inside a backlog that never stopped growing.

Assignments stacked onto quizzes, labs onto presentations, and somewhere between all of it, FYP2 continued lurking in the background asking whether I had truly done enough.

Plagiarism checkers seemed fine, AI ones aren't too... bad/good. Some trimming here, some rephrasing there, and a bit of improvements so it feels more academic.

Groupmates, some are good, some are... not. Communication is good with some, but with others, it's like pulling teeth to get them to reply, and when they do, it might as well not have been a valid reply.

The trimester is entering its final phase now. No more warmups. No more room to drift.

The big weightage and stress bois are arriving. Soon, the end of continuous assessments, start of final assessments.

Ironically, the month’s most stressful event wasn’t even academic.

The Ryzen 5 5600 saga somehow perfectly summarized May itself:

Stuck in customs limbo, endless back-and-forth with sellers and support, expecting the money and package to disappear into the void...

Only for it to suddenly arrive anyway, soaked by rain like it had barely survived the journey. Hurt, but intact.

Honestly, relatable. Akin to my current situation, no matter what happens, eventually it will arrive as long as one keeps pushing forward.

That’s what this month feels like: barely making it through systems that don’t care whether you break or not.

And yet, somehow, things still move forward.

A mini update for the month as well: managed to finally let Homuhomu go as a sale. At long last after 740 days.

Got back around RM80 out of the RM180 paid for it. No more hiding it, but personally — it hurts a bit.

Though, selling it off to someone who'd actually use or appreciate it feels better than just letting it rot or thrown away somewhere.

June approaches fast now, with July proceeding immediately after.

3 Tests. 5 Projects. 6 (or 7) Presentations. And top it all off with FYP2. Physically standing there for 3 hours, with an A1 poster, without a script.

The final obstacle course before the finish line. And eventually... an actual job.

I don’t know if I’m prepared, be it physically, mentally, emotionally, or financially.

But at this point, momentum alone might be enough to carry me through, as long as I play it right.

No matter if I'm prepared or not, eventually, I will have to face all of this and arrive at the finish line.

title: It's all ending.
description:
June didn’t end in resolution — it ended in motion.

Everything stayed stacked: quizzes, tests, projects, presentations, FYP2 breathing down the back of my neck.

But unlike earlier months, it felt less like being crushed and more like being carried forward by inertia.

Not peace, but momentum, as if everything only resolves once I push through.

The first week had a boss rush of 2 tests + 1 presentation assignment. Then a slightly chiller stretch of mostly proposal submissions...

...Followed by a week with just 1 Test. Which was just breathing space for the next boss rush of 2 presentations back to back + 1 quiz. In a single day.

At times things were hectic, other times so peaceful, that I forgot I had things to submit.

Meals stayed the same — familiar stalls, familiar prices, familiar seats. For the most part that is.

The consistency became less of a routine and more of an anchor.

Between deadlines and interviews, food was the only thing that still followed predictable rules.

Some were nice data entries, but there were occasional ones that made me second guess and question reality.

Speaking of interviews, some were chill, some were grilled, some were negotiated into later slots, and the rests... ghosts.

Nothing that gave me an offer, but interviews kept coming, and the pipeline keeps moving.

"Please, please. It's too much winning. We can't take it anymore." Well, an interview is still an interview, so I take it.

Some days were controlled. Some days were improvised. Most days were just “get through it and move on.”

Pre-planned meals? Mostly. Occasional bad ideas, but ah well. Life do be like this.

The interviews didn’t fix anything, but they marked something — a reminder that the end of this phase is no longer abstract.

It is scheduled. It is approaching. Employment. Job. Taxes. Responsibility. Words that strike fear even to the strongest warriors.

Words that somehow carry more weight than the deadlines themselves.

Presoft arc all over again, just with a way longer timeline of no end.

Do I feel ready for July? To be frank, not really. It'd come no matter whether I consent to it or not.

But one things for certain: Do the best I can, and slay this chapter. Once and for all.

title: Mission Complete?
description:
July wasn't the hardest month.

It was simply the last... I hope.

The first week disappeared into FYP2 presentation preparations, poster printing (twice), last-minute fixes, and wondering whether months of work would hold together for those few minutes in front of the panel.

Then... it was over.

(I say this as I played Arknights in front of both of them, though they did came 1 by 1. Quite OK really.)

For general projects, apart from needing to babysit some people, and a late submission... meh.

No more rushing between lectures and labs or tutorials.

No more wondering what next week's assignment would be.

No more checking whether another unsubmitted quiz had silently appeared, or if groupmates are missing progress or communication.

For the first time in years, my timetable became empty.

The interviews kept coming, be it single round, multi round, online, or physical.

Each one a reminder that one chapter was closing while another was already waiting.

The uncertainty never disappeared—it merely changed form.

Silences and rejections? They'd became the norm now, as I'm tasked with a case study I semi signed up for.
Instead of worrying about grades, I now worry about offers, careers, and whether everything I've built will be enough.

This month quietly closed many things.

The moldy wardrobe that had followed me 2 years through university was finally gone.

Lakefront became another place in memory rather than somewhere I needed to return to weekly.

Housemates? From physical people into online people I may never see again, but maybe graduation time we'd meet again.

One by one, routines that had felt permanent simply... ended.

I don't know my results yet. (At least until the 13th, tentatively)

I don't know whether I'll officially graduate on time.

I don't know where I'll be working in a few months (or if I'll be at all).

But I do know this.

I made it to the end.

Four years ago, university was an unknown world.

Now, every cafeteria, shortcut, classroom, and parking lot has become a memory attached to a meal, a deadline, or a conversation.

Whether I passed or failed, whether life immediately improves or throws another obstacle...

This chapter is complete.

The next meal I log won't be as a university student.

It'll be as someone stepping into whatever comes next.

title: So... What Now?
description:
Afterthoughts, Aug 29:

And so, the waiting game began.

The Valiram experience had already given me a pretty good taste of what the working world could look like, but apparently that wasn't enough suffering for one lifetime. Had some free food, met some nice people, and somehow walked away with a Bath & Body Works perfume from Valiram Day.

So at least I got something out of it.

Then came the interviews.
More interviews.
Technical interviews.
Case studies.
Live coding.
Waiting (while applying for more).
Ghosted.
More waiting (while applying for more, and lowering standards).
Rejected.

Some went well.
Some went... well, they happened.

Admittedly, the FB post I made was doing most of the hard carry, but even then, most of these were already stuffed into June and July, while I was still juggling the final stretch of university and all the general academic shit that came with it.

My usual bois grouping had also been forcibly dismantled, so I had to roll for new groupmates.
They weren't necessarily bad, but going from "here's your task, I'll do mine" to actually having to coordinate everyone was certainly an adjustment.

And with different people came a different kind of uncertainty.

Would they actually do their part?
Would I have to babysit them?
Would their performance end up dragging my results down?

My usual group was basically a guaranteed 3.50+ CGPA lobby.
Now I had to put my faith in a completely different set of people, while having considerably less control over how they performed.
And that was... concerning.

Then, around mid-July, I finally reached the point where there was nothing left I could do about it.
I could only wait for the results.

And then the Sakiko plush finally arrived (the one featured as cover icon of the month).

5 August.

The plush I mentioned back in June.
The one that I could've brought to my FYP presentation like the other kids.
The one that arrived after the FYP presentation.

Of course.

Some people got to bring their plushies to their FYP presentations, such is the life of Gen Z.
Mine decided to wait until the entire thing was already over.

Excellent timing.
Absolutely immaculate, cinema, even.

At least Sakiko made it home.

And then the confirmation came.

I passed.

Not only did I pass, I somehow managed to hit the goal I had been chasing for years.

3.50 CGPA.

A number that had spent half my university life sitting just out of reach.

3.15.
3.23.
3.35 (I've hit my first ever 4 flat here).
3.49 (just a bit more).
3.49 (ok maybe if i worked a bit harder).
3.48 (ouch).

And then somehow, finally:

3.50.

During my internship applications, I had gotten so used to selecting "3.00 - 3.49" whenever an application asked for my CGPA that seeing "3.50+" sitting there felt almost unreal.
Not a 4.00.
Not first class (in MMU it's 3.67).
But I didn't care.

I fucking made it.

University was officially done.

Well.
Almost.

There was still the job problem.

The interviews continued.
The case studies continued.
The applications continued.

Then came the physical interview.
A proper, face-to-face interview.
Apparently this was the part where they wanted to determine whether I was actually a human being they could tolerate working with.
Cultural fit, they called it.
Surely nothing could go wrong.
They even offered me a drink on the house.
And then...

I waited.
And waited.

And somehow there were still more interviews.
At this point I had accepted that the job hunt was simply my new trimester.
Except this trimester didn't have a timetable, as it was up to the interviewers, whether they read my resume, and whether they thought I was worth interviewing over the hundreds of other potential candidates.

Some have 4.00 CGPAs.
Okay. Fair enough. They worked harder than I did.

Some have 4.00 CGPAs and several hackathon wins.
Meanwhile I was spending half my weekends travelling home because apparently university has a hidden “maintain your living situation” side quest.

Some have all that, plus multiple internships at big MNCs. The big bois everyone knows.
Citi ("Ah, the bank").
L'Oréal ("Ah, the cosmetics company").
PwC ("Ah, the accounting company").

...Um.
Why are you applying here? I thought this was supposed to be the part where I had a chance.

And then there are the ones who have all of that, plus founded companies (& gotten funding), led teams, won awards, and apparently decided that graduating wasn't enough of a side quest.
At that point, I give up. I'm not even competing anymore.
I'm just observing.
Let me learn from you.

Mom help me I'm scared.
Can I restart university and stay there forever?
I think this guy is secretly three people under one IC.

Still, I kept going.

Then one day, the message came.
"Congratulations, you're hired, here's the offer letter."

...
Oh.
"Sign here, please. We will onboard you on 2nd September."

cue Dr. Facilier getting dragged away

And just like that...

I'm employed. Me. Employed.
The guy who practically lived in Discord since 2017.
Farming pp since 2018.
Closersmaxxing since 2019.
The guy who only started properly learning how to code after picking up the basics through AHK in 2021, just to Closersmaxx more effectively.
The guy who chose a Computer Science degree because it allegedly pays well + gets him access to a gaming laptop.
The Lord Junn, employed?
What happened?

Somehow, all of that led here.

I have a job.

A proper, full-time, permanent job.
Signed.
Done.

No more "hopefully."
No more "maybe."
No more wondering where I'll end up after graduation.
I know.

The degree is done.
The CGPA is done.
The FYP is done.
The internship is done.
The job hunt is done.

So, I suppose this is where Food-MMU ends.

Not because I've stopped eating.
Not because the adventures are over.
But because the chapter this site was born from has finally closed.

Four years ago, this was just a place to keep track of food, and my thoughts on them.
Now it's a record of four years of my life. The highs, the lows, the rants, the updates, the memories.

And honestly?

That's pretty fucking cool.

I don't think I ever expected a food log to become this.
A timeline of where I was, what I was doing, what I was worried about, and who I was at the time.

Some months were good.
Some were shit.
Some were expensive.
Some were lonely.
Some were chaotic.
Some somehow managed to be all of the above.

But they're all here.

49 months later, I can actually look back and see the entire thing.

From the first RM183.30 in August 2022...
to the final RM25.83 in August 2026.

From worrying about food expenses...
to worrying about assignments.
Then internships.
Then FYP.
Then graduation.
Then jobs.

And now?

I'm employed.

What the fuck.

So...
It's all over, huh?

Thanks for reading.

Welcome to the other side.
